notes:
Conditions are stricter about what they will act on — and about what they will refuse.

A follow-up to the last build. Crisp now only skips an edit when your condition means one measurable thing about the file: its shape, whether it has sound, how long it is, its resolution. Words that could mean two things no longer decide — "if it is HD" and "if it is quiet" were each cancelling edits people had genuinely asked for. And a condition you put at the START of a sentence now covers the whole sentence, so "if it's vertical, mute it after trimming to 10 seconds" no longer trims a landscape clip.
